Jonas — good questions. Past plays that worked for similar multi-account pilots:

- Use a single "payer account" private offer in AWS Marketplace. We create the private offer with a 3-month subscription term and specify purchaser as the payer account (CloudRx payer). Then add the three linked accounts as permitted subscribers (AWS supports linked-account subscriptions if the payer controls billing). This avoids three separate offers and keeps procurement simple. Note: we should confirm CloudRx’s AWS org structure; if accounts are separate orgs we may need separate offers.

- Pricing: recommend a two-part pilot structure:
  - Flat pilot access fee (one-time) covering reserved baseline capacity for the 90 days (clearly labeled).
  - Usage overlay (per-token or per-invocation) with an agreed ceiling (procurement likes a hard cap).

- Conversion: provide an explicit conversion path in the SOW: after day 75 we begin conversations to convert to an annual commit. Avoid auto-conversion unless procurement insists; instead include a conversion credit applied to the annual contract if they convert within X days.

- Buyer approvals: procurement generally needs the payer account’s legal signatory. For co-sell, we also register the opportunity in the AWS Partner portal (so seller-led co-sell gets credit). Add a HubSpot link to the deal for tracking.

I've attached a sample PO template that our Legal/Finance likes for pilot terms (sample_private_offer_po.docx). I’ll loop Neha to check any billing accounting notes.

— Vanessa
Director, Marketplace Sales Operations

Couple of practical guardrails from the deal desk / commercial side:

- Discounting: cap pilot discounts at 30% list-equivalent. For pilots where we provide reserved capacity, we can go up to 40% but require Sales Ops sign-off. Keeps conversion math sane.

- Ceiling mechanics: propose a pilot with a $35k flat access fee + usage up to $15k (hard cap) for 90 days. That gives procurement a firm $50k ceiling for approval routing. If they prefer usage-only, we recommend a guaranteed minimum spend with a reconciled credit if usage exceeds the min.

- Conversion incentives: offer a conversion credit equal to 50% of the unused portion of the flat fee if they convert to a 12-month committed plan within 30 days of pilot end. That reduces friction for procurement while protecting seller economics.

- AWS approval notes: when registering co-sell, ensure the deal is in the Partner Central with correct account ids; Amazon’s buyer-approval windows typically take 48–72 hours for partner validation, but the private offer signing itself is driven by the payer account's legal approval.

I'll sign off on a final price sheet if Jon needs it. 

— Vivek
Head of Commercial Strategy
